bull_bear.body:
- Industry-leading market share in India's Extra High Voltage (EHV) power cable business, including turnkey projects
- First-of-its-kind VCV (Vertical Continuous Vulcanization) technology in India for manufacturing EHV HVDC cables
- Longstanding experience and strong credentials in EHV cables, reinforced by securing substantial value contracts
- Technical collaboration with NKT GmbH & Co. KG, Germany for 400 kV EHV XLPE underground HVAC cables since 2018
- Phased organic capacity expansion strategy across all voltage grades, improving capacity utilization and cost competitiveness
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geo-political uncertainties and supply chain disruptions — Management explicitly flags that current geo-political uncertainties have reignited concerns on supply chain disruptions, requiring strategic cost management and fiscal prudence to navigate potential global disruptions.
- Execution delays in capacity expansion projects — The MV & EHV cable capacity augmentation project encountered minor delays in full operationalisation due to civil construction delays and other external factors, potentially impacting the timeline for capturing demand.
- Technological and quality obsolescence in EHV segment — The Company is investing in technological upgradation and modernisation of its EHV facility to meet international quality, safety, and environmental standards, indicating a risk of falling behind evolving global benchmarks.
- Margin pressure from input cost volatility — While pursuing cost management initiatives without compromising margins, the Company highlights the need for reduction of scrap, optimal use of raw materials, and efficient inventory control, implying exposure to raw material price fluctuations.
- Concentration risk in domestic market — Exports constituted only approximately 5.59% of total Revenue from Operations, indicating high dependence on the domestic market and limited geographic diversification.
- Capital allocation and execution risk from large organic expansion — The entire growth plan is based on organic expansion with significant capex directed towards capacity augmentation; any misjudgment in demand or project execution could strain returns on invested capital.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Universal Cables Ltd manufactures and sells a wide range of power cables (1.1 kV to 400 kV), wires, conductors, accessories, and quality power solutions like capacitors, capacitor banks, and harmonic filters. It also undertakes turnkey projects for end-to-end power transmission solutions. The company serves domestic and overseas markets, with an industry-leading position in the Indian EHV cable segment.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Power Cables:** LV Power Cables, MV Power Cables, HV Power Cables, EHV Power Cables (up to 400 kV), EHV HVDC Cables (under development)
- **Wires and Conductors:** Flexible Wires, Multicore Flexible Cables
- **Power Quality Solutions:** Capacitors, Capacitor Banks, Harmonic Filters, MV Automatic Power Factor Control Panels
- **Turnkey Projects:** End-to-end cable system solutions

outlook.body:
- Phased organic capacity expansion across LV, MV, EHV power cables, flexible wires, and capacitors to capture growing domestic and overseas demand.
- Technological upgradation and modernisation of EHV cable facility at Satna to meet international quality, safety, and environmental standards, aiming for greater competitiveness and export orientation.
- Strategic cost management and fiscal prudence to navigate geo-political uncertainties and supply-chain disruptions without compromising margins.
- Emphasis on operational excellence: improving capacity utilization, reducing scrap, optimizing raw-material use, and strengthening supply chain for timely raw-material availability.
- The annual report does not explicitly state a dividend policy, buyback, debt reduction, credit rating, or reinvestment philosophy. No capital allocation policy intent is disclosed in the provided text.
- 81% of inputs were sourced sustainably under the Company's Supplier Framework, which evaluates suppliers on quality, pricing, delivery, and environmental/social standards.
- Capex investment of 0.28% in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, including procurement of special test equipment for automatic optical measurement to reduce virgin raw material usage.
- Comprehensive Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy with zero-tolerance approach, applicable to all employees, directors, business partners, and stakeholders.
- 100% of Board and KMPs covered by training on Code of Conduct, compliance, and sustainability; over 60% of employees and workers covered by safety, environmental, and quality awareness programmes.
- Plastic, e-waste, hazardous waste, and other waste (including acid batteries) are responsibly channeled exclusively to authorized recyclers or through OEM buy-back arrangements, with EPR registration in place.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is implementing a phased capacity expansion strategy. A flexible wire and multicore flexible cables facility at Verna (Goa) and a new Low Voltage power cable facility at Satna (M.P.) were commissioned and became operational in October 2025 and March 2026 respectively. The MV and EHV cables capacity augmentation project is partially commissioned and is expected to be fully operational in a phased manner by end of August/September 2026, having faced minor delays from civil construction and external factors. Additionally, a technological upgradation and modernisation of the EHV cable facility at Satna is planned with an outlay of Rs 7300 Lakhs, focusing on precision manufacturing and flexibility to meet international quality, safety, and environmental standards, aiming to enhance competitiveness and export orientation.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained growth expected in the near term supported by capacitors.
- Gradual increase in production capacity to cater to increased demand for products and services.
- Focus on controlling costs and meeting sustainability expectations to expand footprints in domestic and overseas marketplaces.
- Geo-political uncertainties reigniting concerns on supply chain disruptions, being navigated with strategic cost management and resource optimisation.
